41.0.0.en: 1- “Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.”

41.0.1.en: 1- The poor man is the needy and the materially poor, or the sick. He is also the humble who bears pains or distress for the sake of God, and likewise the one who is spiritually needy, that is, who needs the word of God and someone to help him draw near to God. In addition, it refers to David himself, who humbled himself before God and was also sick, and his son Absalom rose against him in revolt. And finally, this poor man is Christ Himself, who humbled Himself by His Incarnation to save us from our sins.

41.0.2.en: 2- Whoever considers, or shows kindness to, or has pity on the poor man, God rewards him by delivering him in the time of trouble. By the time of trouble is meant the day of affliction, and also the day of the last judgment. So God delivers him from troubles and punishment and supports him, and blesses him with unspeakable blessings.

41.1.0.en: 2- “The LORD will preserve him, and keep him alive; and he shall be blessed upon the earth: and thou wilt not deliver him unto the will of his enemies.”

41.1.1.en: Be blessed (yaghtabit): to rejoice and be glad.

41.1.3.en: 1- This verse mentions God's blessings for whoever shows mercy to the poor: God preserves him from all evil, that is, He keeps evil away from him, and even if evil surrounds him it does not harm him, because God protects him, since he did a work of mercy with one in affliction, so God in his affliction rescues him from all evil. And He preserves him also on the day of judgment, for He forgives his sins and gives him to enjoy the Kingdom. And God gives him the spiritual life here on earth, so he enjoys fellowship with Christ, in addition to his obtaining eternal life full of glory.

41.1.4.en: 2- In addition to God's preserving him and his obtaining life, God also gives joy to the poor man on earth, although there are many sorrows surrounding him, but God keeps for him his inner peace, the joy of his heart, and his enjoyment of fellowship with God.

41.1.5.en: 3- Man's enemies are the demons and all the wicked who follow the demons; these want to wrong, and even destroy, the poor man who relies on God, but they cannot, because God protects him and does not give his enemies an opportunity to harm him.

41.2.0.en: 3- “The LORD will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing: thou wilt make all his bed in his sickness.”

41.2.1.en: Will strengthen him: will support him.

41.2.3.en: 1- Among the blessings of sympathy toward the poor is that God supports the merciful man if he is afflicted with some illness, and heals him, and turns his bodily weakness into strength.

41.2.4.en: 2- Also among God's blessings to the merciful man is that He supports him in his spiritual weaknesses and strengthens him, and develops him spiritually. And this strengthening is either by the healing of the body and its comfort in health, or the opposite, the merciful man is exposed to afflictions, so he is not immersed in bodily comfort but lifts his heart to God, and is strengthened spiritually; in addition, God gives this merciful man a smoothed bed, not only on earth but also in heaven, that is, He gives him eternal rest.

41.2.5.en: Be careful to feel for those around you, to sympathize with their needs, to encourage them and to serve them, confident that whoever shows mercy to another, God shows mercy to him. To the extent that you are occupied with the comfort of others, God comforts you, so that you enjoy fellowship with Him.

41.3.0.en: 4- “I said, LORD, be merciful unto me: heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee.”

41.3.1.en: 1- David declares his need for God's mercy, and that he is sick and needs divine healing, and even declares that the cause of his illnesses is his sin, so he asks God's forgiveness. All this shows David's repentance and humility.

41.3.2.en: 2- David asks spiritual healing for his soul, which is more important than bodily healing, for the forgiveness of sin and the purification of his heart is the divine mercy that he asks. By this he is able to feel God and live with Him, and even reach eternity. So whoever shows mercy to another obtains God's mercies, on condition that he is repentant and concerned for the salvation of his soul; but if the wicked man gives alms, that is not enough for his salvation, like the heretics who, if they give alms for the glory of men, it profits them nothing, and they die in their sins.

41.4.0.en: 5- “Mine enemies speak evil of me, When shall he die, and his name perish?”

41.4.1.en: 1- In the previous verse David began by declaring his weakness and his need for forgiveness in clear humility, and after this he declared the cruelty of his enemies, who speak against him with evil words, intending his destruction and extermination. So he suffers from the evil of his enemies, but he ascribes the cause of his suffering first to his sins and weakness, and then adds and complains of the cruelty of his enemies; that is, he holds himself to account before he holds others to account, and inclines to repentance and not to the condemnation of others.

41.4.2.en: 2- Ahithophel's counsel against David and all the words of the wicked for his destruction was a type of what happened with Christ and Judas's betrayal of Him, when he agreed with the priests of the Jews, and they seized Him and crucified Him, and tried to exterminate His name; but Christ rose, and the Apostles preached Him in the whole world (Acts 4:31).

41.5.0.en: 6- “And if he come to see me, he speaketh falsehood: his heart gathereth iniquity to itself; when he goeth out, he speaketh.”

41.5.1.en: 7- “All that hate me whisper together against me: against me do they devise my hurt. 8- An evil thing, say they, is poured out upon him; and now that he lieth he shall rise up no more.”

41.5.2.en: 1- Among the hardest things is for enemies to appear in the form of loved ones, as happened with Ahithophel, who was David's counselor and of course saw him in his illness and weakness; but the subsequent events showed that he had a strong relationship with Absalom, so he would see David's weakness and report it to Absalom, and when Absalom rose against his father Ahithophel joined him and tried to destroy David, but God rescued him. Likewise Judas clung to Christ like the rest of the disciples, and ate with Him, but he went out to carry out his plot, to inform the Jews and have Christ seized. So both of these traitors, Ahithophel and Judas, spoke falsehood, that is, speech against love, which was an attempt to destroy David and Christ, and they devised plots against them.

41.5.3.en: 2- All David's friends who deceived him and joined Absalom took counsel how to destroy David. Likewise the priests, scribes and Pharisees tried to trap Christ in a word and failed, and their aim was to be rid of Christ, so they crucified Him and He died, but He rose on the third day.

41.5.4.en: 3- Those who betrayed David carried out their plots, and Absalom attacked with a great army to destroy David, and they said among themselves that an evil thing had been poured out upon David, and that he would die and not rise up. But God scattered their counsel, so Absalom died and David was saved. So also the priests of the Jews carried out their plots, and crucified Christ, and by this supposed that an evil thing had been poured out upon Christ, and that they had been rid of Him and He would not rise, but they were surprised by His Resurrection on the third day.

41.5.5.en: 4- David used the word “lieth,” that is, sleeps, to declare the possibility of his rising from the dead, and this is what Christ fulfilled when He raised Himself from the dead quickly, like a sleeper who rose from his sleep, and as Christ declared when He raised the daughter of Jairus and said that she was asleep (Mt 9:24), and likewise Lazarus before He raised him (Jn 11:11). And we too shall rise in the Resurrection like one who was asleep and rose from his sleep.

41.6.0.en: 9- “Yea, the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.”

41.6.1.en: 1- David speaks of those who betrayed him, meaning Ahithophel, or any servant among David's counselors who lived with him for many years, and whom he honored, and then turned against him and joined Absalom and drove David out of his kingdom and tried to kill him. And at the same time he speaks in the spirit of prophecy about Judas Iscariot, who was one of Christ's disciples, and betrayed Him and delivered Him to the Jews; so David describes this traitor as follows:

41.6.2.en: A – The man of his peace: that is, he lived in peace with him and was one of those close to him. So that Judas, when delivering Christ up, kissed Him, that is, there was between him and Christ a very warm friendly relationship.

41.6.3.en: B – I trusted in him: Ahithophel was one of David's chief counselors, and likewise Christ entrusted the money box to Judas, and this shows Christ's trust in Judas, that He entrusted him with the money.

41.6.4.en: C – Who ate my bread: Ahithophel was very close to David, and likewise Judas was one of the twelve disciples, and both of them ate at the table of their master. And Christ dipped bread in the dish and gave it to Judas apart from the rest of the disciples, that is, he was distinguished.

41.6.5.en: These three characteristics confirm the Master's love for this traitor, and therefore increase the guilt and heinousness of the betrayal.

41.6.6.en: 2- Of this traitor David said “lifted up his heel against me,” that is, his foot, to trample me and crush me; for Ahithophel's counsel aimed at killing David while he was a fugitive and exhausted. As for Judas, his betrayal led to the crucifixion of Christ and His death, and indeed he sold Him for a paltry sum. All this shows the hideousness of the evil in the traitor's heart.

41.6.7.en: May you value the love of others, and respond to their love with greater love, and not act as a result of pressures you pass through, and so wrong another, especially those who are close, lest you become a traitor to love like Judas.

41.7.s.en: (3) The victory of … for His children

41.7.0.en: 10- “But thou, O LORD, be merciful unto me, and raise me up, that I may requite them.”

41.7.1.en: 1- David asks God to be merciful to him, that is, to rescue him from the plot of the wicked and the traitors, and to heal him of his illness, and this is a declaration of David's humility and his need for God's mercy and help. And it is a prophecy about Christ, who in humility became incarnate, and asked the Father to be merciful to Him, that is, that the divinity support the humanity in the accomplishing of redemption.

41.7.2.en: 2- David asks God to raise him up, so that he may requite the wicked, and exalt and establish justice in the kingdom; he does not seek vengeance on the wicked, but the establishing of justice, since as a king he is responsible for the firmness of justice in his kingdom. And it is a prophecy about Christ, who asks the Father to raise Him up, that is, that the divinity raise the humanity, and requite Satan whom He bound by the Cross, and cast him into eternal torment at the end of the days. And everyone who persists in evil is also cast into hell, for refusing repentance. As Christ requited the Jews who refused to believe in Him, so that they were no longer His people, and their city was destroyed by the hand of the Romans in AD 70, and many of them were killed.

41.8.0.en: 11- “By this I know that thou favourest me, because mine enemy doth not triumph over me.”

41.8.1.en: 1- David rejoiced that God was pleased with him, so King Saul did not triumph and shout over him, nor Absalom, for both died and God saved David from their hands, indeed from all David's enemies from the surrounding countries, and David triumphed and took possession of their lands.

41.8.2.en: 2- The Father declared that Christ is His beloved Son, and was well pleased with Him when He was baptized in the River Jordan. And Satan was not able to make Him fall in the temptation on the mountain, but Christ triumphed over him. Likewise on the Cross the Father smelled His sacrifice as a sweet-smelling savour, and Satan was not able to seize His spirit after His death, but on the contrary Christ seized Satan and bound him, triumphing over him.

41.9.0.en: 12- “And as for me, thou upholdest me in my perfection, and settest me before thy face for ever.”

41.9.1.en: 1- David ascribes the perfection in which he lives to God; it is a grace given to him to walk in the way of perfection, and he thanks God for this, especially since he kept his perfection in the midst of difficult circumstances, such as the enmity of Saul and Absalom toward him. And he thanks God also that He raised him from his sin, and established him in the way of perfection, purity and love in which he will live forever, that is, not only in this present world, but he declares his hope in eternity, in which he remains standing before God in this perfection.

41.9.2.en: 2- This verse applies to Christ, who lived perfect while in the flesh, and said, “Which of you convinceth me of sin?” (Jn 8:46). Then He rose from the dead and raised mankind in Himself to reign with Him forever in the Kingdom.

41.10.0.en: 13- “Blessed be the LORD God of Israel from everlasting, and to everlasting. Amen, and Amen.”

41.10.1.en: 1- David concludes the psalm by glorifying God, the God of Israel, who is worthy of all honor from everlasting to everlasting, forgetting all his sufferings, then asks Him to answer all his requests in this psalm, and confirms this by saying Amen, and Amen.

41.10.2.en: 2- There is an opinion that this verse was added by one of the elders of the Jews at the end of the last psalm of each of the first four sections of the Psalms, but to the fifth and last section of the Psalms this verse was not added, because the last psalms are all glorification of God (see the introduction to the Book of Psalms).

41.10.3.en: God is your supporter, so advance in your spiritual life and your service, and do not be troubled by the wars of Satan, because God is able to give you victory over them. And He is also able to adorn you with many virtues, and then give you the happiness of eternity.

41.10.4.en: God the Disciplinarian and Savior. To the choirmaster, for the sons of Korah - a poem “O God, we have heard with our ears” (v. 1) Introduction:

41.10.5.en: 1- Its writer and the time of its writing:

41.10.6.en: A - The prophet David, when the Edomites attacked the tribe of Judah, while David was occupied at that time with other wars, and they destroyed many of the Jews.

41.10.7.en: B - One of the sons of Korah wrote it in the days of King Hezekiah, when King Sennacherib of Assyria fought him and took possession of many places in Judea, and killed many of them.

41.10.8.en: C - An unknown person wrote it in the days of the Maccabees, when they fought the Greeks and triumphed over them, after the Greeks had destroyed many of the Jews.

41.10.9.en: 2- Its subject: the believing people of God, who rejected idolatry, were subjected to attack from their enemies, but they cried to God, and He rescued them, saved them, and gave them victory in the end over their enemies. So it is a communal prayer of supplication to God, that He may have mercy on His people and not leave them in the hands of their enemies.

41.10.10.en: 3- This psalm suits every person who suffers afflictions and persecutions but holds fast to his faith, so he seeks God with importunity, that He may rescue him and lift his pains from him.

41.10.12.en: 5- This psalm is a prophecy about the Apostles in the Apostolic age, and the martyrs in the ages of the martyrs, who faced many persecutions, but God supported them with miracles and glorified them.

41.10.13.en: 6- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.
